duplicate_or_version_note: The digitized article is the 1985 second edition of work whose first edition was an MIT preprint from 1980; overlap with the frozen parent corpus or other versions was not assessed, so novelty remains unconfirmed.
extraction_risk: The long source has highly usable explanatory prose, but OCR frequently corrupts mathematical symbols, accents, arrows, indices, page headers, and displayed formulas. Exact theorem statements and formula-bearing spans require verification against the typeset pages; edition-specific hypotheses and later-strengthened remarks must not be silently conflated.
mathematical_scope: Bott-localized algebraic K-theory with finite coefficients and its comparison with etale cohomology and topological K-theory, developed through hypercohomological descent, spectral sequences, localization, transfer and induction, splitting principles, and applications in arithmetic geometry.
usefulness_reason: Useful for several explicit, generic conceptual moves: localize an invariant to remove a precisely identified obstruction; bridge a subtle invariant to computable cohomological data through a convergent spectral sequence; prove descent by reducing from schemes to local rings and then fields; propagate a base case using localization, transfer, induction, devissage, and five-lemma arguments; and separate construction, convergence, and comparison gates. The text also explains what information localization forgets and why local-to-global reconstruction is valid under stated hypotheses.
